agentCan: Build the key-entry connect form and secure credential storage
Call the API with Bearer keys and handle key rotation (delete + recreate)
Implement the Event Webhook verification if you receive SendGrid webhooks

approval.trigger: None exists. No app review, no marketplace review, and no user cap appear anywhere in the docs: any SendGrid user can create a key and hand it to any third party immediately. The only gate is whether the customer trusts you with a bearer credential.

blockers.detail: There is no delegated authorization: your product stores a long-lived bearer credential per customer. A key is not tied to your app's identity, and the user revokes by deleting the key, which kills the connection entirely. Your security posture (vaulting, encryption, breach impact) becomes the product question instead of scopes and consent.
blockers.howToClear: Ask for a Custom Access key scoped to only what you use, store it in a real secrets vault, and document rotation for customers.
blockers.title: You hold the customer's credential, not a token

blockers.detail: The first API key for an account must be created in the SendGrid App UI; API-based key management only works after a key with key-management permissions exists. There is no consent flow you can embed to automate onboarding.
blockers.howToClear: Write clear customer-facing instructions (Settings > API Keys > Create API Key, Custom Access) and expect a manual step in every onboarding.
blockers.title: Bootstrap is manual, in the customer's console

sources.label: Event Webhook security features (the reversed-OAuth evidence)

tested: Read-only verification: the API-key model, key types, and the absence of any third-party OAuth/app-registration mechanism were checked against current twilio.com/docs/sendgrid pages (no account created, no key generated)
unverified: The full per-endpoint permission list available under Custom Access keys (the pages read describe the three key types and exclusions without enumerating every category).
Any limit on API keys per account, and explicit key expiry behavior (no expiry is stated; keys appear to live until deleted).
Whether any on-behalf-of/subuser delegation mechanism exists for third parties (none is described in the docs read).
Any partner/integration directory program for SendGrid (none referenced in the docs read).

alternatives: Full Access key (everything except billing and Email Address Validation; broader than most integrations need)
flavor.recommended: No OAuth flavor exists. The documented connection model: each customer creates a Custom Access API key in their own SendGrid account and pastes it into your product
flavor.why: SendGrid's official docs contain no app registration, no authorization endpoint, and no consent screen for third-party apps. API keys are the product's stated authentication model ('a secure way to talk to the API that is separate from your username and password'). Custom Access is the least-privilege option among the three key types.

humanMust: The CUSTOMER creates the API key in their own SendGrid console (Settings > API Keys) and pastes it into your connect form
The customer deletes the key to revoke you
You decide and document the key permissions you ask customers for
name: SendGrid
nuances: The only OAuth in SendGrid's docs runs in reverse: the Event Webhook security feature lets SendGrid obtain a client-credentials token from YOUR authorization server so its webhook calls to you carry a verifiable token. It does not give your app access to users' accounts.
Basic authentication with a real username/password is not supported; basic auth exists only with username 'apikey' and the API key as password.
Non-billing keys cannot touch billing endpoints or Email Address Validation, no matter their other permissions.
The documented compromise playbook is delete the key, create a new one, update environment variables, which underlines that the docs imagine first-party use.
Account 2FA is recommended and its enablement breaks password-based integrations, pushing everything to keys.
prerequisites: A connect form in your product that accepts an API key
Customer-facing instructions for creating a scoped key

steps.detail: Instruct the customer: in their Twilio SendGrid console, Settings > API Keys > Create API Key, choose Custom Access and grant only the permission levels your product uses (Full Access excludes billing and Email Address Validation; Billing Access is billing-only). The first key on an account must be created in the UI.
steps.title: Customer creates a scoped API key

steps.detail: The customer pastes the key into your product's connect form. There is no redirect or consent screen to build; your work is the form plus vault-grade storage.
steps.title: Customer pastes the key into your product

steps.detail: Call api.sendgrid.com/v3 with the header Authorization: Bearer <api-key>. Subsequent keys can be managed via the API once a key with key-management permissions exists.
steps.title: Call the API with the Bearer key

steps.detail: If a key is compromised or a customer leaves: the customer deletes the key in their console (revocation is total, not per-feature), creates a new one if continuing, and updates your stored copy.
steps.title: Rotate or revoke by deleting the key

tagline: There is no OAuth app to create or get approved. SendGrid's connection model is an API key your customer generates in their own console and hands to you, with all the trust trade-offs that implies.

time.active: Minutes: the customer creates a key; you build a key-entry form and Bearer-header calls
time.total: Same day; no registration or review exists to wait on
